state.misconception_label: Does not understand that 2n represents an even number

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: I have: Which of these shows part of the proof that the sum of two odd numbers is even? I got \( \begin{array}{l}2 n+(2 m+1) \\ =2(n+m)+1\end{array} \) because I'm not sure I worked it out the right way.

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: There is a specific procedure for this. Step 1 is to identify the operation; step 2 is to apply the rule for that operation. Keep in mind that when adding two odd numbers, the result will be even.

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: Wait, but you just wrote the same thing I got... so was my answer actually right? I'm confused because you said the sum of two odd numbers should be even, but that expression ends with +1, which makes it odd, doesn't it?

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: I'm still confused though... you keep saying the answer should be even, but the expression ends with +1, which I thought made it odd? Like, if I have 2(n + m) + 1, isn't that always going to be odd because of the +1 at the end?
